# PatternTable

Table pattern for PLUS design system. Table shell: table children (consumers pass their own thead/tbody), a pagination slot under the rows, and an empty-state slot. The table has no toolbar of its own: the Section header above it carries the title, search, filters and actions. With `empty`, the header stays and the empty state takes the body as one message row spanning every column, so the columns still say what will appear. The table itself is no-fill (transparent): the surrounding card or surface provides the background, and row states are layered over each cell's fill rather than replacing it. - **Row states**: hovered and pressed rows take the neutral subtle steps; a row with `aria-selected="true"` (in a `role="grid"` table) takes the selected ladder across the whole row, with no stripe on its leading edge; the row's checkbox is the cue that does not rest on color. - **Sticky cells**: `stickyHeader` pins the head row and `stickyColumn` the first column. They paint the current surface, so they match the page or the card they sit in, and take the overflow shadow only while content is scrolled under them. `stickyHeader` pairs with `maxHeight`: only a bounded region scrolls vertically, so without `maxHeight` the header is not pinned. A bounded region, or one with a sticky column, takes keyboard focus so it can be scrolled without a pointer. Mirrors the "Table" slot component in the Figma design system file.

Also asked as: list of records, data table on a page, sortable list, records with filters.

## Usage

A table sits in a Section and spans it. Its first and last cells sit flush with the section edge. The Section header carries the toolbar and the tabs: search, filters, the record count and the bulk bar use the toolbar type, and saved views use the tabs type. Empty, no results, loading and error states happen inside the table, under its header, so the Section header stays usable. Paging stays under the rows, inside the same Section.

### Type guidance

Pick the type from what people do with the rows. Ask the questions in order, and stop at the first yes.

| Question | Type |
| --- | --- |
| Does any row nest under another? Nesting wins, even when the table is interactive. | Tree table |
| Can people act on the table: sort, filter, select, page, expand rows or use row actions? | Dynamic table |
| Otherwise, people only read it. | Static table |

Search, filters and actions sit in the Section header: `<PatternSection toolbar={<PatternSection.Toolbar />}>`.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name every column with a short head, in sentence case: "Last session". | A blank head, or one in all caps. |
| Give the count in words in the toolbar: "340 students". | A count in the head row or under the table. |
| An empty message that says what will appear and the first action: "No members yet", "Invite a member". | An empty table body with no message. |

## Best practices

### Put a plain table in a Section. {#put-a-plain-table-in-a-section}

Do: The table spans the Section under its header: no frame, no card, no padding of its own.
Don't: The table sits inside its own frame with padding. It stops lining up with the Section and the Section header.

### Put nothing between the header and the head row. {#put-nothing-between-the-header-and-the-head-row}

Do: Search, filters and the record count live in the Section header toolbar. The head row follows directly.
Don't: A second toolbar sits between the Section header and the head row. The table has no toolbar of its own.

### One table per block. {#one-table-per-block}

Never mix a Static, Dynamic or Tree table in one Section either.

Do: One table per Section, with its own header, so people always know which rows a toolbar acts on.
Don't: Two tables share one Section and one header. The toolbar no longer says which table it acts on.

### Use a Dynamic table for rows people act on. {#use-a-dynamic-table-for-rows-people-act-on}

Do: A roster people act on as a Dynamic table: sortable heads, checkboxes, a pager, and bulk actions in the Section header.
Don't: A roster people act on as a Static table. With no sort, selection or paging, 340 students become one long scroll.

### Use a Tree table for a hierarchy. {#use-a-tree-table-for-a-hierarchy}

Do: Classes nest under their school and students under their class. Each level indents and keeps the columns.
Don't: A hierarchy faked with expandable rows: the classes and students lose their columns and can't be sorted or selected.

## Accessibility

- Name every column with a head cell. Head cells are labels for a column, so they use Heading/xxsmall rather than a heading level.
- Mark the sorted column with `aria-sort`, and give every icon-only control a name, such as "Actions for Ava Thompson".
- Mark a selected row with `aria-selected="true"`. That attribute belongs to a row of a table with `role="grid"`.
- Selection is never color alone. The row's checkbox is checked, and the toolbar says "2 selected".
- A region that scrolls takes keyboard focus, so people can scroll it without a pointer. That covers a region with `maxHeight` and one with a sticky column.
- The empty message is a row of the table, so assistive technology reads it with the columns it replaces.
- Name the table through `tableProps`, such as `aria-label`, when no caption names it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | — | — |
| `pagination` | node | — | Pagination slot under the rows; hidden while the empty state shows |
| `emptyState` | node | — | Empty-state slot: a message row under the head row, spanning every column, when `empty` is true |
| `empty` | bool | `false` | Swap the body rows for the empty-state message row; the head row stays |
| `stickyHeader` | bool | `false` | Pin the head row while the rows scroll under it; needs `maxHeight`, since only a bounded region scrolls vertically |
| `stickyColumn` | bool | `false` | Pin the first column while the other columns scroll under it |
| `maxHeight` | number or string | — | Bound the scroll region's height (number of px or any CSS length); a sticky header pins only within it |
| `tableProps` | object | — | Props for the `table` element itself: an accessible name, a class a wrapper styles it by |
| `className` | string | `''` | — |
| `style` | object | — | — |
| `children` | node | — | Table content slot — pass thead/tbody elements |
